sections.html: The African Glass Catfish, Parailia pellucida, is always available and fits perfectly in any community tank. The maximum length is given as 15 cm in the literature; however, specimens larger than 8 cm are only very rarely seen. Available size: 6-8 cm.
They are completely undemanding in respect of water hardness and pH; any water that is suitable as drinking water for humans will do.
They are peaceful plankton feeders. The fish feed readily on any type of usual fish food.
They are peaceful and should always be kept in company of their own kind. The fish love well planted tanks with a good number of places to hide and not too strong lighting.

The African Glass Catfish is not a close relative of the Asian Glass Catfish. The latter belongs to the family Siluridae, which also contains the European Wels (Silurus glanis), whereas the African species belongs to the family Schilbeidae. The best known Asian Glass Catfish is Kryptopterus vitreolus. The similar look and behaviour are due to a similar lifestyle and environment, not a genetic relationship, comparable to birds and bats, which both have wings but are not close relatives.

P. pellucida can be easily recognised by the presence of an adipose fin (absent in Kryptopterus) and eight long barbels around the mouth (only two in Kryptopterus).
